▽ More
Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. Existing
general
-purpose benchmarks (e.g., MMLU and HELM) primarily assess broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but fail to capture critical domain requirements such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality. This gap is particularly concerning in fitness and health applications, where incorrect or unsafe recommendations can lead to physical harm. To address this limitation, we introduce MoveBench, the first comprehensive benchmarking framework specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching. The proposed benchmark integrates heterogeneous task formats, including multiple-choice
questions
(MCQs) and
open
-
ended
question
answering (OpenQA), grounded in real-world user scenarios and paired with structured rubrics emphasizing safety compliance,
scientific
validity, and training logic. Through large-scale evaluation of 15 diverse LLMs on 809
questions
with 5,012 rubric-level criteria, our results reveal substantial performance variability, particularly in safety awareness, structured program design, and personalization capability, highlighting a critical gap between knowing and doing. Our work establishes a foundational evaluation standard for sports and health LLM applica…

Drug
discovery
requires continuous
scientific
decision-making across a vast research space. We introduce PharmAgents2, an
autonomous
system for end-to-end drug
discovery
that combines knowledge-enhanced decision-making with organized large-scale exploration. Paper2Skill extracts transferable
scientific
decision knowledge from public sources and, together with expert-developed skills, supports research decisions. Self-Scaling
Discovery
expands exploration through parallel
agents
inheriting research context and decision-making capabilities across targets,
scientific
hypotheses, and
discovery
strategies. We introduce PharmAgents-Bench v0.1, comprising 121 questions across nine decision scenarios and three end-to-end tasks assessed with expert-defined process rubrics. PharmAgents2 outperforms evaluated baselines in most decision categories and achieves the highest process scores on all three end-to-end tasks. In three real-world studies,
autonomous
investigations generated findings subsequently supported by human-executed experiments. For LpxH, PharmAgents2 hypothesized a previously unreported allosteric site and screened compounds against it, identifying a novel inhibitor scaffold with experimentally confirmed inhibitory activity and binding.
